name: Survodutide
summary: An experimental Boehringer Ingelheim drug that activates glucagon and GLP-1 receptors, in phase 3 trials for obesity and fatty-liver disease; it is not FDA-approved.
what_it_is: Survodutide (BI 456906) is a lab-made drug that switches on the receptors for two hormones, glucagon and GLP-1. Boehringer Ingelheim licensed it from Zealand Pharma and is testing it for obesity, type 2 diabetes and MASH (fatty-liver inflammation) with liver scarring. It is investigational and not approved.

evidence.why: Two phase 3 randomized trials (725 and 755 adults) reported by Boehringer Ingelheim, which says both were published in NEJM, plus a published phase 2 trial of 387 adults; results on heart outcomes and long-term safety are not yet available.

status_us.label: Investigational; not approved
status_us.note: Survodutide is in phase 3 trials and holds FDA Fast Track (2021) and Breakthrough Therapy (2024) designations for MASH; no FDA filing was announced in the sources checked. FDA has warned companies selling survodutide falsely labeled 'for research purposes' or 'not for human consumption.'

benefits.claim: Average weight loss of up to 16.6% over 76 weeks versus 3.2% with placebo in 725 adults with obesity or overweight without type 2 diabetes (company-reported)
In 755 adults with obesity or overweight and type 2 diabetes: up to 13.1% weight loss versus 3.1% with placebo, and A1C down by up to 1.21 points versus 0.03, over 76 weeks (company-reported)
Less liver fat: in a 48-week trial of adults with fatty liver disease and excess weight, 61.0% reached normal liver fat versus 5.7% with placebo (company-reported)

risks.risk: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and constipation, mostly while the dose was being raised: 18% to 19% stopped because of digestive side effects versus 1.2% to 2.9% with placebo
In the phase 2 trial, 91% had a side effect versus 75% with placebo, and 75% had digestive side effects versus 42%
Long-term safety and effects on heart events are not yet known; a heart-outcomes trial had not reported in the sources checked
Survodutide sold online as a 'research' product is unapproved, and FDA has warned sellers
Approved GLP-1 drugs carry a boxed warning about thyroid C-cell tumors in rodents; whether this applies to survodutide was not reported in the sources checked

avoid_if: Anyone outside a clinical trial: it is not an approved medicine
Personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer or MEN 2 (approved GLP-1 drugs carry this contraindication)
interactions: Not well studied. Approved GLP-1 drugs raise the risk of low blood sugar with insulin or sulfonylureas and slow stomach emptying, which can change how oral medicines are absorbed

before: General health check: weight, blood pressure, HbA1c or fasting glucose, kidney and liver tests
during: Same general checks at regular visits
labs.why: No evidence-based monitoring exists outside clinical trials because it is not approved; these are general health checks, with heart rate added because the label of an approved GLP-1 drug (semaglutide) calls for it.

studies.title: Glucagon and GLP-1 receptor dual agonist survodutide for obesity: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-finding phase 2 trial
studies.people: 387 adults with overweight or obesity, without diabetes
studies.finding: Over 46 weeks, weight fell 6.2% to 14.9% across doses versus 2.8% with placebo; side effects affected 91% versus 75%, mostly digestive.

studies.title: Positive data from two Phase III SYNCHRONIZE obesity trials
studies.people: 725 adults with obesity or overweight, without type 2 diabetes (SYNCHRONIZE-1)
studies.finding: Up to 16.6% average weight loss at 76 weeks versus 3.2% with placebo; 19% stopped because of digestive side effects versus 2.9%. Company-reported.

studies.title: Boehringer Ingelheim's survodutide achieves up to 13.1% weight loss in new Phase III trial, alongside significant improvements in glycemic control in people with obesity and type 2 diabetes
studies.people: 755 adults with obesity or overweight and type 2 diabetes (SYNCHRONIZE-2)
studies.finding: Up to 13.1% weight loss versus 3.1% and A1C reductions of up to 1.21 versus 0.03 points at 76 weeks; 18% stopped because of digestive side effects versus 1.2%. Company-reported.

notes_for_editor: Phase 3 results come from Boehringer Ingelheim releases (June 7 and October 1, 2026) that cite NEJM papers (le Roux et al., doi 10.1056/NEJMoa2600751; Wharton et al., doi 10.1056/NEJMoa2607219), which were not opened. The weight figures are 'efficacy estimand' results (as if everyone stayed on treatment), which typically run higher than treatment-policy results. About 1 in 5 stopped because of digestive side effects. Heart-rate effects were not reported in the sources opened and are worth checking in the papers. SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT results were expected later in 2026. FDA's GLP-1 page names survodutide among 'research' products it warned about but does not separately address compounding. Class cautions come from the Wegovy label, not survodutide data.
